Security review of PR #298, ROUND 2 / FINAL under C34.

Verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES, following the prime's disposition relayed by pm-001. No additional normal-use security bug was found in the scoped decoder, injection, caret, cross-user and override review. This is not a claim that every destructive absence case is fixed: F248 remains open.

|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| F248 / R298-R2-001 | 🟠 HIGH | crates/testkit/src/tmux_sweep.rs | 289-300 | A disappeared bound-parent alias is ignored, so a still-live socket can be classified stale and unlinked. | 10/10 |

F248 is accepted for the next small PR, not a blocker to this merge under the prime's C34 ruling. F247 is folded into that follow-up. Fleet --apply remains HELD: neither this verdict nor the merge authorizes the F241 production sweep. The security holding is retained until merge.

Security-specific receipts:

- The helper executed 24 focused checks using nice -n 19 python3 - and the native Bash 3.2, extracting the decoder/seam expressions from the exact R2 source. The justfile SHA-256 was 61f7755717438275dee25435bd16698a3481eb3916065e96a1055ada1fc7af5f.
- Nine decoder checks passed: command substitutions, backticks, semicolons, quotes, parameter-assignment text, percent formats, literal backslash-c, literal backslash-x2f and option-like names remained data. No command, format, option or recursive-backslash evaluation occurred. The printf format and destination variable are fixed; the decoded name is quoted in filesystem tests (justfile:844-848).
- Fifteen caret/seam checks passed. Three ambiguous caret names refused without changing either override. Unset/empty PIJ_BOUNCE_LSOF selected /usr/sbin/lsof; an explicitly supplied /bin/false remained the selected seam value. PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE values unset, empty, 0, true, on, 01 and whitespace-padded 1 refused; only exactly 1 overrode. These were parsing/selection probes, not execution of a substitute lsof or a bounce.
- Static review confirms LC_ALL=C and the absolute default at justfile:821, the explicit-only UNSAFE gate at :865, and Rust caret rejection at tmux_sweep.rs:407,412. Socket names do not set or evaluate PIJ_BOUNCE_LSOF/UNSAFE. Those environment seams remain trusted same-user inputs under C33, not an isolation boundary.
- Cross-user handling was inspected, not tested by impersonating another user: unknown or same-user ancestor ownership retains uncertainty at tmux_sweep.rs:311, while candidate ownership is checked by ours (:203) and the socket/lock guards (:507-538). The distinction for another user's inaccessible directory is part of the reviewed policy, not a general proof for arbitrarily relocated bindings. F248 below is the concrete remaining unresolvable-parent failure.
- Candidate checks retain symlink_metadata and lock O_NOFOLLOW; holder metadata lookup intentionally follows paths to identify device/inode. No new credential disclosure or publication of raw holder records was identified in the delta. Internal absolute proof paths are omitted from this public verdict.

Independent correctness receipts supplied by bee and inspected here, not rerun by security:

- review298-r2-probes/case-0-baseline.log: six regressions passed, covering escaped names, Linux space-path replay, alias identity, unresolved paths, parse/exec failure and unknown orphan locks. results.json records exit 0. Three sweep guard mutations returned the expected exit 101.
- review298-r2-alias/runtime.json: a real tmux server with 128 backlog clients returned ECONNREFUSED (61). Differently spelled paths had identical device/inode. The exact R2 refusal branch rejected the live holder; replacing inode matching with textual equality removed the refusal. No live bounce ran.
- F248, review298-r2-live-table/result.log and result.json: all paths from a real lsof census fed the exact-source proof crate. Removing only the bound-parent symlink left the listener live, but the sweep reported Stale and removed 1. The expected-retained assertion failed, exit 101. Production source-prefix SHA-256: cd9ff875d45e4406a4e6864cb0bf44304d0da5ba82819ce62733fb01b5fee128. All destructive actions stayed in owned scratch.

F246 is unchanged in the R2 delta. The R1 pre-cargo stamp/lock receipts still apply to that unchanged code; they do not prove zero source-mtime side effects, because source touching precedes the guard.
